source_review.notes: Checked all eight references for identity, authority, revision or publication date, and bounded claim scope. OpenTelemetry Specification 1.60.0 supports span context, parent, link, kind, event, status, lifecycle, sampling, processing, and export claims. The W3C Trace Context Recommendation dated 2021-11-23 supports interoperable HTTP propagation, validation, mutation, privacy, and security claims; Level 2 is identified as separate draft work. Current OpenTelemetry semantic-convention pages are cited with their per-convention stability limitation. The 2010 Dapper and 2007 X-Trace primary papers support historical architecture and causal-propagation claims. Current OpenTelemetry sampling and Collector scaling guidance supports head/tail trade-offs and trace-affine routing for stateful processing. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined the trace graph, span identities, optional parent, links, half-open intervals, duration, kind, resource, outcome, direct-child set, interval measure, controlled expected and observed sets, completeness, sampling strata, and inclusion probability before formal use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Checked set-builder notation, graph edges, union measure, products, ratios, probabilities, percentages, interval boundaries, and every TeX delimiter for GitHub rendering.

evidence: Recomputed Example 2 child lengths 60 and 50 ms, overlap 20 ms, union 90 ms, and root exclusive time 30 ms.
Recomputed Exercise 2 union [20,130) plus [150,180) as 140 ms and root exclusive time as 60 ms; naive individual subtraction gives 30 ms because 30 ms overlap is double-counted.
Recomputed independent retention 0.1^8 as 0.00000001, one in one hundred million.
Recomputed weighted sampling example as 100 errors and 9,900 successes, yielding 1% error rate.
Executed trace-interval-model under CPython 3.14.4 with five exact output lines, empty stderr, and zero exit.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Every numerical conclusion is bounded to stated independence, clock, containment, completeness, or known-probability assumptions.

evidence: Checked that unique IDs, at-most-one parents, parent resolution, one root, and acyclicity are separately required for a rooted collected tree.
Derived exclusive time by interval-union measure and checked the overlap inclusion-exclusion step.
Derived all-span independent retention as the product of per-span probabilities and equal-probability special case q^n.
Checked controlled completeness and inverse-probability weighting under nonempty known expected sets and positive known inclusion probabilities.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No claim equates collected structure with semantic truth, wall interval with CPU time, timestamps with causality, or weighted retained traces with an unbiased estimate under unknown loss.

evidence: Reviewed missing and invalid parents, multiple roots, cycles, zero duration, overlapping children, child outside parent, clock skew, retries, timeout, cancellation, fan-out, fan-in, batches, late spans, long workflows, streaming, message redelivery, exporter loss, backend rejection, tail-state split, overload, untrusted context, large baggage, secrets, personal data, and tenant access.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Absence, incompleteness, deliberate trace restart, unsupported propagation, sampling exclusion, and downstream loss remain distinguishable where evidence permits.

evidence: Traced valid unpredictable identity, acyclic primary ancestry, explicit links, extract-scope-inject lifecycle, stable operation names, semantic kind and outcome, exactly-once span end, retry and asynchronous boundaries, disclosed sampling, bounded context, and observable collection loss through exposition, code, examples, and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: The tracing system is treated as a lossy production dependency with its own capacity, privacy, and reliability obligations.

evidence: Reviewed parent-graph, overlap, sampling, causality, critical-path, and absence-of-evidence arguments.
Verified assumptions for comparable clocks, contained intervals, direct collected children, independent inclusion, known probabilities, semantic message edges, and complete dependency relationships.
proof_review.notes: Proof-like conclusions are structural or conditional; no universal completeness, authenticity, performance, causal reconstruction, or critical-path guarantee is asserted.

evidence: Audited ground truth, complete, causal, ordered, critical, exclusive, valid, authentic, sampled, recorded, exported, accepted, indexed, retained, secure, private, stable, and compatible; mechanisms, assumptions, policies, and limitations are explicit.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The executable block is labeled a deterministic interval model rather than a general tracer or critical-path analyzer.

evidence: Executed trace-interval-model under CPython 3.14.4 and confirmed 3 spans, 1 root, 120 ms root duration, 90 ms child union, and 30 ms root exclusive interval.
All gateway, payment, queue, batching, collector, sampling, and adversarial-carrier cases are explicitly hypothetical or controlled examples.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live tracing SDK, application, message broker, collector cluster, backend, production trace, or user traffic was exercised.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed trace boundaries, span identity and lifecycle, parent versus links, operation semantics, synchronous and asynchronous propagation, timing, concurrency, retries, status, events, sampling, pipeline loss, cost, privacy, testing, and interpretation limits.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed operational failures from context breaks, false parenting, unended spans, raw-path naming, clock skew, overlapping intervals, fragmented sampling, late spans, collector rebalancing, queue overflow, export rejection, sensitive baggage, tenant leakage, and tracing-induced latency. Internal practitioner review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from trace vocabulary through graph and lifecycle mechanisms, six bounded arguments, one executable interval model, nine trade-offs, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, ten cross-program connections, and five progressive exercises with complete corresponding answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Specifications, primary papers, deterministic calculations, and hypothetical examples do not establish production trace completeness, semantic correctness, causal truth, unbiased sampling, sufficient capacity, privacy, security, or service reliability.
